correctness.rationale: PASS: First CTMC outbreak infects a connected cyclic interval when size<n, and its conditional location is uniform by rotational symmetry; residual susceptible vertices form a path. Along a unique path of length d, d independent source-vertex races transmit with probability p^d (no false assumption that two edges out of the same infected vertex are independent). Averaging over all susceptible new seeds and vertex targets yields 1+2/L Σ_d (ℓ−d)p^d per path component. For random immunes exactly n*C(n−d−1,k)/C(n,k) oriented d-edge segments survive; each unique residual path pair is counted exactly once. Coefficients are strictly positive by ∏_{j=1}^d(1−(k−1)/(n−j))<1. Hockey-stick summation at p↑1 gives (k−1)(L−1)/(k+1); dominated convergence and k=2 Riemann sum yield the three limiting regimes, with all boundary restrictions explicit. Independent exact Fraction enumeration of every k-immune subset and every susceptible index on cycles n=4..11 at p=1/3,1/2,3/4 reproduced the polynomial. The packaged CTMC first-step recursion was separately inspected but its logged results are not used as the proof.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualifying well-established qualitative phenomenon: Ueki–Thompson–Banaji (Jan20 2026) and Hiraoka et al. already analyze differences in infection-acquired versus random immunity and topological localization. The reviewed materials do not give the identical conditional fixed-k finite homogeneous-cycle CTMC formula, coefficientwise strict inequality, exact saturated bound, or two scaling regimes and k2 crossover. Another 2026 cycle study concerns two high-contact independent percolation edges, and 2026 vaccination study independently seeds many vertices; neither implies the fixed-k conditional SIR law. Literature priority of possible one-dimensional percolation formulations remains a risk.
residual_risks: The qualitative localization disadvantage is prior art and not novel; a one-dimensional exact network reliability/percolation formula in an unindexed appendix could subsume some coefficients.
The claim does not apply to arbitrary networks or unequal source recovery dependencies, nor infer clinical recommendations.
The original first primary outcome includes conditional cluster shape only, not conditioned path-seed distribution across heterogeneous individuals.

value.rationale: PASS: Quantifying protection differences at the same immune count isolates topology from prevalence, a natural network-epidemic comparison. The full finite-n positive-coefficient polynomial and exact fixed-k versus proportional-k and near-perfect transmission crossover capture distinct population regimes. The statement is an exact model theorem with clear scope, not an empirical clinical forecast or a generic statement that clusters are different.

final_claim: For CTMC SIR on simple cycle C_n, n>=4, condition first outbreak on exactly k infections, 2<=k<=n−2, and compare its contiguous immune block with uniformly random k immunes: for fresh uniform susceptible seed and p=β/(β+γ), exact positive-coefficient gap is 2/(n−k) Σ_{d=1}^{n−k−1}[(n−k−d)−n C(n−d−1,k)/C(n,k)]p^d, with exact p→1, fixed-k, proportional-k, and k=2 critical scaling laws.
limitations: Simple homogeneous CTMC cycle, exactly k prior infections, uniform new seed, permanent immunity, positive β and γ; no arbitrary graphs or biological calibration.
Finite checks prove no unrestricted statement; proof's pair counting/clock races/dominated convergence carry generality.
